prompt: A user types the ocean freight line as a percent of CIF on the invented BADAGRY build-up. What does landedCost return?
options: REFUSED: Customs processing has an unknown stage "customs".
REFUSED: The insurance rates on CIF add up to 100 percent or more.
REFUSED: Ocean freight is a percentage of a value that is not formed until after freight.
REFUSED: An FOB price and its basis are required.
explanation: Freight belongs to the freight stage, and CIF is formed at the insurance stage, after freight. The engine refuses a freight line that names a value formed later, and prints the same sentence for freight on C&F.

prompt: A charge is added to the invented BADAGRY walk with its stage typed as "customs". Which answer does landedCost give?
options: The line is placed in the landed stage, the nearest stage the walk knows, and billed on CIF.
REFUSED: Customs processing has an unknown stage "customs".
REFUSED: Ocean freight is a percentage of a value that is not formed until after freight.
REFUSED: The insurance rates on CIF add up to 100 percent or more.
explanation: The walk knows the stages freight, insurance and landed. A line with any other stage has no place in the order and so no frozen base, and the engine does not guess that customs means landed.

prompt: Insurance is quoted on CIF at 100 percent in a test of the invented BADAGRY walk. What happens?
options: The closed form divides by zero and the engine prints a CIF of none beside a complete build-up.
REFUSED: Ocean freight is a percentage of a value that is not formed until after freight.
The engine moves the insurance onto C&F, the basis the template ships, and completes the walk.
REFUSED: The insurance rates on CIF add up to 100 percent or more.
explanation: CIF = (C&F + any other insurance) / (1 - the sum of the CIF rates), and at 100 percent the denominator is zero. The engine refuses the call with the sentence above and forms no CIF.

prompt: The course's invented import duty of 5.75 percent prints 1399086.04 USD on BADAGRY. Which figure is it a percent of?
options: The landed total, 26513943.86 USD
explanation: Duty ships as percent_of_cif and bites on CIF as frozen at the end of the insurance stage. It sees none of the landed lines, which come after CIF is fixed.

prompt: The invented regulatory rate of 0.0024 USD a litre prints 109854.60 USD on BADAGRY. Which quantity is it levied on?
options: The 45772.752 bill-of-lading m3
The 45772751.75 bill-of-lading litres
The 34000 bill-of-lading tonnes
The cargo as one unit, whatever its size
explanation: The regulatory line is per_litre, so it reads the litres. The per_m3 lines read the m3, the per_tonne lines the tonnes, and per_cargo is a flat charge such as the 52500.00 USD demurrage.

prompt: The invented demurrage provision of 52500 is typed as per_cargo. What does that basis do to the amount?
options: The rate is multiplied by the 34000 tonnes, as the port line's rate is.
The rate is read as a percent of CIF.
The rate is the charge: 52500.00 USD whatever the cargo's size.
The rate is spread over the 45772.752 m3 and billed per cubic metre.
explanation: A per_cargo line reads no quantity at all. It is levied once, and the walk prints it as 52500.00 USD.

prompt: Insurance on BADAGRY at the invented 0.16 percent is quoted first on CIF and then on C&F, every other invented rate unchanged. Which CIF does each build print?
options: 24331931.09 USD on CIF and 24331868.80 USD on C&F.
24331931.09 USD in both builds, since the rate is unchanged.
24331868.80 USD on CIF and 24331931.09 USD on C&F.
24293000.00 USD in both builds, since C&F is frozen first.
explanation: The comparison table prints CIF 24331931.09 USD with insurance on CIF and 24331868.80 USD with it on C&F. 24293000.00 USD is the C&F of the walk priced with insurance on CIF.

prompt: Insurance on BADAGRY moves from the invented 0.16 percent of CIF to the same rate on C&F. Why does the import duty line change as well?
options: The duty is a percent of the insurance line, so any change in the premium passes through it.
The engine re-solves every percentage line in closed form whenever an insurance basis changes.
The duty is a percent of C&F, and moving the premium onto C&F changes that base.
The duty is a percent of CIF, and CIF has changed with the insurance.
explanation: The duty reads CIF, which prints 24331931.09 USD with insurance on CIF and 24331868.80 USD with it on C&F. So the duty prints 1399086.04 and 1399082.46 USD.

prompt: How does landedCost reach a CIF of 24331931.09 USD when the invented insurance is quoted as a percent of CIF?
options: By iterating: guess a CIF, charge the premium on it, and repeat until the figure stops moving.
By charging the premium on C&F, the base the template ships, and adding it to C&F once.
It refuses, since a charge on a base that contains itself is a forward reference.
By one division: CIF = (C&F + any other insurance) / (1 - the sum of the CIF rates).
explanation: The engine uses the closed form. Iterating the fixed point is how the independent oracle reaches the same CIF, which is why the two figures agreeing means something.

prompt: The invented duty and financing rates are left blank on BADAGRY. What does landedCost report?
options: complete false, missing Import duty and Financing and letter of credit, total 24774210.79 USD, labelled a floor.
A refusal naming the duty, since a percent of CIF with no rate leaves the walk unable to form CIF.
complete true, total 24774210.79 USD, with the two blank rates read as zero and listed in assumedZero.
complete false with a total of 26513943.86 USD, the last complete build, until the two rates are typed.
explanation: The engine adds what it was given, names what it was not and labels the sum. It prints "A FLOOR: 2 rate(s) not supplied, so the full landed cost is at least this." beside 24774210.79 USD.

prompt: On BADAGRY the course's invented duty is typed 0 in one build and left blank in another. Both totals print 25114857.82 USD. What tells them apart?
options: Nothing the engine prints, since a blank and a zero produce the same figure on every row of the walk.
The duty line, which prints zero dollars in the typed build and a refusal in the blank build of the walk.
The complete flag and the missing list: true with none missing, against false with Import duty missing.
The total, which the blank build marks as none because the walk cannot close on a missing duty.
explanation: The totals match, so the difference sits in the flag and the list: a rate typed 0 is a rate the engine applied, and a blank is a rate it names as missing.

prompt: With every invented rate left blank, landedCost prints a total of 23392000.00 USD. What is that figure?
options: The landed cost, complete true, with every blank rate read as zero.
The FOB alone, labelled as a floor with 9 rates missing.
The C&F value, since freight is formed from the FOB price.
The CIF value, formed before any landed charge applies.
explanation: It is the same figure as the FOB line of the full build. The engine prints it with complete false, 9 rates missing and "A FLOOR: 9 rate(s) not supplied, so the full landed cost is at least this."

prompt: The course prints 26513943.86 - 24774210.79 = 1739733.07 USD for BADAGRY, every rate invented. Which lines does the floor build leave out of its total?
options: The invented import duty and the invented financing line, both percents of CIF.
The invented port and jetty lines, both levied on the bill-of-lading quantity of the cargo.
The invented insurance and freight lines, both formed before CIF is frozen.
The invented storage and demurrage lines, both booked at the landed stage.
explanation: The floor build is the one with the duty and financing rates blank. The full build prints them at 1399086.04 and 340647.04 USD, and the floor names both as missing.

prompt: Why can the invented import duty on BADAGRY never bite on the storage bill of 121297.79 USD?
options: Storage is per m3 and a percentage line can only read a per-tonne base.
The engine adds every percentage line last, after the per-quantity lines.
Storage is billed to the terminal and the duty only reads the importer's lines.
Duty reads CIF, which is frozen before the walk reaches any landed charge.
explanation: Each base is frozen when the walk reaches it. The duty's CIF of 24331931.09 USD is formed at the insurance stage, before any landed charge, and the financing line, also a percent of CIF, prints ahead of demurrage in the walk.

prompt: A corrected density arrives for the BADAGRY cargo. Which invented landed line does the walk leave untouched?
options: Jetty throughput and discharge, levied per m3.
Storage and handling, levied per m3.
Port and harbour charges, levied per tonne at 103700.00 USD.
Regulatory and inspection charges, levied per litre.
explanation: FOB and port are both formed from the 34000 tonnes, and a tonne is a mass. Jetty and storage read m3 and the regulatory line reads litres, and those volumes pass through the density.
